capabilities: Update links, display text included, when a note is renamed or moved
Move a note's attachments with it, folder and all
Rewrite HTML src and href paths and report paths stored in other plugin settings
Clean up a deleted note's attachments and the folders left empty
Confine the plugin to part of the vault with include and exclude path lists
disambiguation: Not a bulk or pattern-based file renamer; it manages what happens to links, attachments and folders when a note is renamed or deleted.
extras: Documentation is a demo vault shipped with each release and readable on GitHub; the plugin stands aside while an older plugin that owns its own rename/delete handler is enabled, and exposes an API so other plugins can hand over their rename and delete settings.
intentEvidence: Obsidian updates the links pointing at a note when you rename it, and stops there.
problem: Obsidian updates links when a note is renamed but leaves its pasted attachments under the old name, and deleting a note leaves those files orphaned in folders named after nothing.

relations.evidence: Same lifecycle goal; arbitrary existing layouts; shared attachments; include/exclude paths
Alternative grouping: derives attachments from links and configured folders
Broader sweep: whole vault, deepest first, in one command
Ensure you have the BRAT plugin installed and enabled.

summary: Vault-wide rename and delete handler that keeps links, attachments and folders consistent, and cleans up what a deletion leaves behind.
